title: Israel and Lebanon ceasefire agreement takes effect
body:
A ceasefire agreement between Israel and Lebanon was signed on 26 November 2024 and took effect on 27 November at 02:00 GMT, ending about 14 months of fighting between Israel and Hezbollah. The United States and France were the mediators. Hezbollah was not a signatory, but Lebanese parliament speaker Nabih Berri negotiated with its support. Israel's security cabinet approved the deal by a vote of 10 to 1, with National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir opposed. President Joe Biden called the arrangement "designed to be a permanent cessation of hostilities."

The agreement provided for a 60-day halt to hostilities. Israel was to withdraw its forces from southern Lebanon in phases, coordinated with the deployment of the Lebanese army. Hezbollah was to move its forces north of the Litani River, and the Lebanese Armed Forces were to be the only armed presence in the area south of the river. A monitoring mechanism chaired by the United States, with France taking part, was created, and both sides kept the right of self-defence.

On 26 January 2025 the US extended the withdrawal deadline to 18 February. After that deadline Israel withdrew from populated areas but kept five positions along the border. Lebanon's Health Ministry said Israeli attacks killed at least 83 civilians in the early period of the truce, while Israel said dozens of Hezbollah fighters were killed. The Lebanese health ministry and the United Nations reported in November 2025 that more than 330 people, including 127 civilians, had been killed by Israeli forces since the ceasefire began. Israel said its strikes targeted Hezbollah fighters or imminent threats.
